name: Catppuccin Mocha
why: The most ported palette in every source checked (official palette, YASB gallery, HyDE, HyprPanel, JaKooLit, windots on real Windows). Soft pastels on a deep blue-grey work with acrylic.

name: Catppuccin Latte
why: Best-supported light theme; same accents as Mocha so users can flip day and night with one switch.

name: Rose Pine
why: Already has matching Windhawk taskbar and Start menu themes, so it is the most native Windows result; muted purple and rose reads calm.

name: Rose Pine Dawn
why: Warm paper-like light variant; reuses the Rose Pine taskbar and Start layout with the light palette.

name: Tokyo Night
why: Omarchy's default and a top unixporn palette; deep navy with bright blue and violet accents suits a floating top bar.

name: Nord
why: Low-contrast arctic blues that sit well next to stock Windows apps; YASB has a ready Nord theme with light and dark modes.

name: Gruvbox Material Dark
why: Warm retro earth tones; dedicated YASB theme exists and the palette is easy on the eyes for long sessions.

name: Everforest
why: Green, nature-toned and gentle; YASB everforest theme covers light and dark.

name: Kanagawa
why: Ink-painting palette (deep indigo, parchment text, muted gold); distinctive without being loud.

name: Dracula
why: Very well known, high-contrast purple and pink; many users will look for it by name.

name: Matte Black
why: Minimal near-black monochrome with a single warm accent; professional and distraction free.

name: Edge Runner (Cyberpunk)
why: Neon yellow on black, inspired by Cyberpunk 2077; dedicated YASB theme and HyDE theme exist, strong gamer appeal.

name: Synthwave '84
why: Retro neon pink and cyan on purple; a fun showcase look that photographs well.

name: Flexoki Light
why: Ink-on-paper light theme, very readable in bright rooms; gives users a second light choice that is not pastel.

name: Oxocarbon
why: IBM Carbon inspired: neutral greys with pink and cyan accents; crisp and modern, fits a productivity audience.
